newsitem.title: JAPAN: North Korea says ready for more peace talks.
newsitem.headline: North Korea says ready for more peace talks.

text.p: North Korea is ready to join in proposed four-way peace talks and looks forward to more preliminary sessions with the United States and South Korea, its top negotiator said in a statement on Thursday.

"It is our stand to hold 'four-way talks' for peace and security of the Korean peninsula," Vice Foreign Minister Kim Kye-gwan said in a statement carried by the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) and monitored in Tokyo.

"We, therefore put forward a way of realising the talks in our reply briefing. In order to make the talks more effective and productive, we proposed to have more rounds of negotiations among the DPRK (North Korea), the United States and South Korea before beginning the 'four-way talks'," Kim said. The fourth participant in the talks is China.
Kim heads North Korea's delegation at the preliminary round of talks held in New York. The latest round began last week but ended after the chief South Korean negotiator flew back to Seoul on Monday.
Kim's statement was the first North Korean reaction since the talks were suspended.
The aim of the preliminary rounds is to start full-fledged negotiations for a peace treaty to replace an armistice that ended the 1950-1953 Korean War.
Kim urged the United States to adopt more confidence-building measures, in an apparent reference to famine-stricken North Korea's demands for more food aid from Washington.
"Confidence needed for 'four-way talks' has not yet been built between the DPRK and the U.S. and, still worse, our equal footing at the talks has not been guaranteed," Kim said.
North Korea has complained that while South Korea has diplomatic ties with both China and the United States, Pyongyang has no diplomatic ties with Washington.
